sources.excerpt: Skinner Box – Stomp Under Foot Skip to content Search Search Cart PRODUCTS CONTACT FAQ DEALERS ARTISTS ABOUT BLOG Skip to product information Previous Next Close SKINNER BOX™ Regular price $199.99 By Stomp Under Foot Quantity Add to cart Inspired by the rare 1978 “Bud Box” Rat, the Skinner Box has a gain range that goes from fat distortion to a chewy, low-gain overdrive, with a slightly fuller response from the metal can LM308 for a smoother feel. Known mainly as a distortion, it also works great as an overdrive. With the gain set between 11 and 12 o’clock, it delivers a clear, balanced overdriven tone that responds to your picking and cleans up with your guitar’s volume. The low end stays tight, chords stay defined, and single notes cut without getting harsh. Stomp Under Foot browse by type distortion/fuzz/overdrive distortion browse by enclosure pedal Stomp Under Foot Skinner Box Published on December 7, 2012 Stomp Under Foot distortion pedal Information Stomp Under Foot Last year I was thinking of doing a pedal based on the original 1978 Rat distortion pedal. I wanted to do this because I always missed my original big box pedal and I have a bunch of the original LM308 chips. Recently I revisited this idea and started making some different versions and comparing them. I felt that the original version had the best overall. The Skinner Box will be limited to the amount of LM308 chips I have. Once the LM308s are gone I won't be making the pedal any more. Also, I am using as many original parts as I can find in these but my main goal is to just make it sound right. The original pedal has a reputation for being an 80s metal pedal but it is so much more. True, it was used to push Marshall amps to create the 80s metal sound but put it into a nice clean amp with the Distortion at 9-10 o'clock and the tone about 1 o'clock and you get a dirty yet clear and snappy bluesy tone. For a great medium gain rock tone put the Distortion about 12-1 and for a full distortion on the verge of fuzz turn the gain up to 3-4 o'clock.
